name: Memory Inhibition
description: Retrieving some memories can make related competing memories harder to recall later. Remembering is not only strengthening; it can also suppress neighboring traces.
design_relevance_note: Only weakly relevant to mainstream product UX, but potentially useful in learning tools, search/knowledge systems, reminders, and repeated cueing patterns where surfacing some items may crowd out related alternatives. This is much more a cognitive-memory mechanism than a standard designer shorthand.
prevalence_note: Mostly academic memory language; rare in mainstream design practice outside learning-science or knowledge-system discussions.

findings.description: Meta-analytic review of retrieval-induced-forgetting studies supports a real pattern in which retrieving some items harms later recall of related competitors, consistent with inhibitory retrieval processes rather than pure strengthening alone.
findings.source_title: Forgetting as a consequence of retrieval: A meta-analytic review of retrieval-induced forgetting.
